//Serilog: The EF Core command override is the only real change from appsettings.json. Locally the generated SQL is worth seeing; it stays at Warning everywhere else, because one line per query at Information is a volume problem in production and, with `Include Error Detail=true` in the connection string, a data-exposure one. Keep explanatory `//` keys OUT of MinimumLevel:Override — Serilog reads every key in that block as a logger name and every value as a level, so a comment there fails to parse as a LogEventLevel, is then treated as a LoggingLevelSwitch reference, and throws while the host is being built.

SocialProviders.//: Local-only OAuth fixtures for the endpoint workbench. SocialAuthService also checks that the host environment is Development, so this flag cannot enable demo identities in staging or production.

//ConnectionStrings: NOT set here, on purpose — a connection string carries a password, and this file is committed. Development reads ConnectionStrings:Postgres from user-secrets (`dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:Postgres" "..."`), other environments from the ConnectionStrings__Postgres environment variable (§25). Startup fails with a named error if neither is present. Add `Include Error Detail=true` to your local secret if you want Npgsql to put parameter values in exception messages — useful locally, a data leak anywhere else.
